name: Jasmine Moreau
life: “I still remember unlocking a school library while the streetlights were on.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Jasmine by a small Monday habit. Jasmine usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I am the cleaner who opened the library early. I kept my copy inside the first book she asked to borrow.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. Jasmine has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Jasmine looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Jasmine has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To keep the class picture in the child's favorite book.
family: Ren Ruiz is Jasmine’s second cousin. Jasmine saves a place. Ren chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The kitchen without a boss*, Ren says, “I have wanted this job for years. I learned on day two that the deliveries call before the children wake.”
connections: Marlowe Nunes. The library copy and the bicycle drawing are two ways a helper can receive thanks.

reactions.situation: A recipient wants to say thanks without being pictured
reactions.response: Jasmine offers a written reply or an ordinary visit without requiring a photograph in return.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Jasmine starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Jasmine says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
